missing-number.d: An array holds n distinct numbers from [0, n]. Return the one missing number.
missing-number.i: XOR all indices 0..n with all values; pairs cancel (x ^ x = 0), leaving the missing number. Equivalent: n(n+1)/2 - sum.

most-stones-removed-with-same-row-or-col.d: A stone can be removed if another remaining stone shares its row or column. Return the maximum number of stones that can be removed.
most-stones-removed-with-same-row-or-col.i: Stones sharing a row or column form connected components, and each component can be reduced to one stone. Answer = n - number of components (union-find).

move-zeroes.d: Move all zeros to the end in place, keeping the order of the non-zero elements.
move-zeroes.i: Write pointer: for each non-zero element, swap it into position w and increment w. Zeros naturally drift to the end.

n-queens.d: Place n queens on an n x n board so none attack each other; return all board configurations.
n-queens.i: Place one queen per column with backtracking. A cell is safe if its row, its anti-diagonal (row+col) and its diagonal (n-1+col-row) are unused; boolean arrays make the check O(1).
k: Backtracking scanning the board for safety

network-delay-time.d: A signal starts at node k in a weighted directed graph. Return the time until all nodes receive it, or -1.
network-delay-time.i: Single-source shortest paths with non-negative weights: Dijkstra with a min-heap. The answer is the maximum shortest distance, or -1 if some node is unreachable.

next-greater-element-i.d: For each value in nums1 (a subset of nums2), find the first greater value to its right in nums2, or -1.
next-greater-element-i.i: Compute next-greater for all of nums2 with a monotonic stack (right to left), store it in a map value -> next greater, then look up each nums1 value.

next-greater-element-ii.d: Next greater element for every position in a circular array.
next-greater-element-ii.i: Simulate two copies of the array: iterate i from 2n-1 down to 0 using nums[i % n] with a monotonic stack, and only record answers when i < n.

next-permutation.d: Rearrange the array into the next lexicographically greater permutation, in place (wrap to the smallest if it's the last).
next-permutation.i: 1) From the right, find the first i with nums[i] < nums[i+1] (the pivot). 2) From the right, find the first element larger than nums[i] and swap them. 3) Reverse the suffix after i. If there's no pivot, reverse the whole array.
k: Pivot, swap with successor, reverse suffix

non-overlapping-intervals.d: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap (touching endpoints are fine).
non-overlapping-intervals.i: Greedy: sort by start; on overlap, remove one and keep the interval with the smaller end (it leaves more room). Sorting by end and counting non-overlapping intervals is equivalent.
k: Sort by start, keep the smaller end on overlap

number-of-1-bits.d: Count the set bits in an integer's binary representation.
number-of-1-bits.i: Check each of the 32 bits with a mask. Faster trick: n &= (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so loop until n == 0.

number-of-islands.d: Count the islands (4-directionally connected groups of '1') in a grid.
number-of-islands.ex: a grid with 3 separate land blobs -> 3
number-of-islands.i: Scan the grid; each unvisited land cell starts a new island. Flood-fill it (DFS or BFS) so its cells aren't counted again. Mark cells visited when you enqueue them, not when you dequeue.

number-of-operations-to-make-network-con.d: Move cables between computers to connect the whole network. Return the minimum number of moves, or -1 if impossible.
number-of-operations-to-make-network-con.i: Union-find: every edge joining two already-connected nodes is a spare cable. With c components you need c-1 cables, so the answer is c-1 if spare >= c-1, else -1. (Shortcut: if edges < n-1, answer -1.)
k: Union-find counting extra edges and components

odd-even-linked-list.d: Reorder a linked list so all odd-position nodes come first, then even-position nodes, keeping relative order. O(1) extra space.
odd-even-linked-list.i: Keep two chains (odd and even) and remember evenHead. Advance odd.next = even.next and even.next = odd.next alternately, then attach evenHead to the end of the odd chain.
k: Build a new list in two passes

pacific-atlantic-water-flow.d: Water flows to neighbours of equal or lower height. Return the cells from which water can reach both the Pacific (top and left edges) and the Atlantic (bottom and right edges).
pacific-atlantic-water-flow.i: Reverse the flow: DFS uphill from every Pacific border cell and from every Atlantic border cell, marking what each ocean can reach. Return the cells marked by both.
k: Reverse DFS from both ocean borders

palindrome-linked-list.d: Return whether a singly linked list reads the same forwards and backwards.
palindrome-linked-list.i: O(1) space: find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half, and compare it with the first half node by node.
k: Find middle, reverse second half, compare
Copy values to an array + two pointers

palindrome-number.d: Return whether an integer reads the same backwards (negatives are never palindromes).
palindrome-number.i: Reverse the digits arithmetically (rev = rev*10 + x%10) and compare. Reversing only half the digits avoids any overflow risk.

palindrome-partitioning.d: Return all ways to split s so that every piece is a palindrome.
palindrome-partitioning.i: Backtracking: from index start, try every end where s[start..end] is a palindrome, add it, and recurse from end+1.

palindromic-substrings.d: Count the palindromic substrings of s (by position).
palindromic-substrings.i: Expand around each of the 2n-1 centres; every successful expansion step is one more palindrome.

partition-equal-subset-sum.d: Can the array be split into two subsets with equal sums?
partition-equal-subset-sum.i: If the total is odd, it's impossible. Otherwise it's subset-sum to total/2 (0/1 knapsack): canMake(i, t) = canMake(i-1, t) || canMake(i-1, t - nums[i]).

partition-labels.d: Split s into as many parts as possible so each letter appears in at most one part. Return the part sizes.
partition-labels.i: Record each letter's last index. Scan, extending the current part's end to max(end, last[c]); when i == end, close the part.
k: Remaining-count map, close when all seen counts hit 0
